#3725

A bare `-> dict` now gets the same structured output as `-> dict[str, Any]`, and a bare `-> set` / `-> frozenset` is wrapped in `{"result": ...}` like their parameterized forms. A bare `-> list` / `-> tuple` deliberately stays unstructured, and `structured_output=True` now wraps it instead of raising.

## Motivation and Context

Bare builtins fell through to the "other class" branch of `_create_output_model`, where `get_type_hints(dict)` is `{}`, so the tool silently got no `outputSchema` and no `structuredContent`. With `structured_output=True` it raised `return type <class 'dict'> is not serializable`, which reads as if a dict weren't serializable.

| Annotation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `-> dict` | no schema | `{"type": "object", "additionalProperties": true}`, unwrapped |
| `-> set`, `-> frozenset` | no schema | wrapped, `{"type": "array", "uniqueItems": true, "items": {}}` |
| `-> list`, `-> tuple` | no schema | no schema (on purpose); wrapped with `structured_output=True` |

### Why bare `list` / `tuple` stay unstructured

`_convert_to_content` renders content blocks found in a list or tuple as blocks, and `_returns_content` already opts `list[ImageContent]` and friends out of structured output so the image isn't also echoed into `structuredContent`. A bare `list` says nothing about its items, so it may hold blocks too: a `-> list` tool returning `[Image(...), {...}]` would send the image twice, once as a block and once as base64 in `structuredContent`. Some clients then render the JSON instead of the picture, others put the base64 in the model's context. `set` / `frozenset` can't hold content blocks (they aren't hashable), so wrapping them is safe.

FastMCP made the same call (`function_parsing.py`: bare `list`/`tuple` produce no output schema for this reason, while bare `dict` and `set` get one). `list[X]` and `structured_output=True` remain the explicit opt-ins.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- Bare `list` / `tuple` added to `test_content_block_return_annotation_yields_no_output_schema`.
- `test_structured_output_true_wraps_a_bare_list`, `test_a_bare_list_inside_a_union_keeps_its_schema`, `test_a_bare_dict_is_structured_like_dict_str_any` and `test_a_bare_set_is_wrapped` snapshot both `output_schema` and the full `CallToolResult`.
- Full suite passes; coverage 100%, `strict-no-cover`, ruff and pyright clean.

## Breaking Changes

Tools annotated with a bare `dict`, `set` or `frozenset` start publishing an `outputSchema` and validating their result against it, exactly as `dict[str, Any]` / `set[Any]` do today. Values that used to be dumped as text with `to_json(..., fallback=str)` and now fail as a tool error (`is_error=True`):

- a bare-`dict` tool returning non-`str` keys, e.g. `{1: "a"}`;
- a `None` return from a `-> dict` / `-> set` tool;
- a value pydantic can't serialize to JSON, e.g. an instance of an arbitrary class inside the dict or set.

Bare `list` / `tuple` tools are unchanged unless they pass `structured_output=True`, which used to raise. Only a bare `list` / `tuple` as the whole annotation is opted out; nested ones (`list | None`, `dict | list`, `list[list]`) keep the wrapped schema they publish today.

## Additional context

This differs from the branch proposed in #3725, which also wraps bare `list` / `tuple`; the reason is the double-send above. Unparameterized `typing.List` / `typing.Tuple` are unchanged (still wrapped like `list[Any]`).
